facts.statement: The only valid species, Nanantius eos, was first described in 1986.
facts.quote: The only valid species of Nanantius is Nantantius eos,' which was first described in 1986.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found at Warra Station near Boulia in Queensland.
facts.quote: This holotype tibiotarsus (QM F12992) was found at Warra Station near Boulia, in Queensland.

facts.statement: Evidence of Nanantius being seabirds includes a tibiotarsus found in the gut of an ichthyosaur specimen QM F16811.
facts.quote: The theory that Nanantius were seabirds is evidenced by the fact that another tibiotarsus referable to this genus, and quite possibly to N. eos itself, was found in the gut of an ichthyosaur with specimen number QM F16811.

facts.statement: Nanantius eos has been classified as an enantiornithean, a group of primitive Cretaceous birds that did not survive the mass extinction.
facts.quote: Nanantius eos has been classified as an enanthiornithean, a Cretaceous group of primitive birds that did not survive the Cretaceous–Paleogene mass extinction.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Nanantius belongs to Enantiornithes because its tibiotarsus characters are not sufficiently diagnostic.
facts.quote: However, it is now known that the characters of the tibiotarsus are not sufficiently diagnostic to place a bird into the Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Nanantius is tentatively placed in a clade closely related to Vorona, Grabauornis, and Yungavolucris.
facts.quote: Nanantius is tentatively recorded as part of a clade closely related to Vorona, Grabauornis and Yungavolucris.

facts.statement: Nanantius is classified within the family Alexornithidae.
A supposed second species, Nanantius valifanovi, was found to be a synonym of Gobipteryx minuta.
facts.quote: Una supuesta segunda especie, Nanantius valifanovi, resultó ser un sinónimo de Gobipteryx minuta.

facts.statement: In 1997, additional fossils from Canary Station in Australia were assigned to the genus Nanantius.
facts.quote: En 1997, otros fósiles procedentes de Canary Station, en la misma zona de Australia, también fueron clasificados dentro del género Nanantius.

facts.statement: A partial left tibiotarsus (QM F31813) was assigned to Nanantius but excluded from N. eos due to anatomical differences.
facts.quote: El otro hueso era un tibiotarso izquierdo parcial (QM F31813) que se asignó a Nanantius pero no se incluyó dentro de Nanantius eos debido a que poseía algunas diferencias anatómicas.

facts.statement: Nanantius inhabited the Eromanga Sea and its surroundings, a large inland sea in what is now Australia, during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Conocido y datado del Cretácico Inferior (Albiano, hace aproximadamente 100-112 millones de años), habitó el Mar de Eromanga y sus alrededores, un gran mar interior en lo que hoy es Australia.

facts.statement: The fossil record of Nanantius spans from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (106.3 to 100.5 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Until the description of the contemporary Tenuicruris in 2026, Nanantius was the only named bird genus from the Cretaceous of Australia.
